description: A four-panel composite figure mixing two dual-axis scatter plots, one bar chart and one schematic. (a1) and (a2) are titled "M1 Steel Composition" and "M2 Steel Composition": x-axis Annealing Temperature (°C) (~580-900), left y-axis "Calculated Retained Austenite Fraction at RT (%)" scaled 0.0-1.0, right y-axis "Ms Temperatures (°C)" 0-400. Filled grey squares track the left axis (retained austenite), open diamonds the right axis (Ms, marked by an arrow). A pale shaded band labelled "Complete Retention of Predicted Equilibrium Austenite fraction" ends at a vertical dashed line near 650 °C; a horizontal dashed line sits just above 0.0. In both panels the filled squares fall with increasing annealing temperature (M1 from ~0.4 to ~0.05; M2 from ~0.27 to ~0.05) while Ms climbs to ~300 °C. (b) "Grain Size Distribution": bar chart, Frequency (%) 0-100 vs Grain Size (μm) 0.0-3.0, black = M1, red = M2; ~95% (M1) and ~92% (M2) of grains fall between ~0.25 and 0.5 μm, with M2 showing a small (~3%) population near 1.5 μm. (c) "Intercritical Annealing & Partitioning" schematically shows γ, α, δ-ferrite and partitioning arrows. Together they argue that above a critical intercritical annealing temperature the predicted equilibrium austenite cannot all be retained, and that grain refinement and Mn/C (M1) or extra Si (M2) partitioning raise measured retention above the calculated value.

subfigures.description: Dual-axis plot for M1 steel. Filled squares (left axis, calculated retained austenite fraction at RT) decrease from ~0.4 at ~600-650 °C to ~0.05 at 900 °C; open diamonds (right axis, Ms temperature) rise from below the 0 °C dashed line near 650 °C to ~300 °C at 900 °C. A shaded band on the left, labelled "Complete Retention of Predicted Equilibrium Austenite fraction", is bounded by a vertical dashed line near 650 °C.

The same dual-axis construction for M2 steel. The filled squares (retained austenite fraction) are lower, starting near 0.25-0.28 at 600-650 °C and falling to ~0.05 at 900 °C; the open-diamond Ms curve rises to ~300 °C. The same shaded complete-retention band and ~650 °C vertical dashed line and the horizontal RT dashed line are drawn.

Bar chart, Frequency (%) (0-100) vs Grain Size (μm) (0.0-3.0), legend M1 = black, M2 = red. Nearly all grains lie in the ~0.25-0.5 μm bin (M1 slightly higher, ~95%, than M2, ~92%); a small 0.5-1.0 μm population (~5% M1, ~7% M2) and, for M2 only, a ~3% bin near 1.5 μm.

Schematic of intercritical annealing and partitioning with legend: red arrow = Mn, C; black arrow = Si. Left ("Actual Partitioning of M1"): red arrows carry Mn and C from white α into the orange γ region beside a large pink γ grain. Right ("Actual Partitioning of M2"): the same Mn/C red arrows into γ plus black Si arrows leaving γ into both α and a blue stacked δ-ferrite region.

observations.observation: Panels (a1) and (a2) plot Annealing Temperature (°C) on x against two y-axes: left "Calculated Retained Austenite Fraction at RT (%)" (0.0-1.0) and right "Ms Temperatures (°C)" (0-400).
In (a1) the filled-square retained-austenite points fall from about 0.4 at ~600-650 °C to about 0.05 at 900 °C, while the open-diamond Ms curve rises to about 300 °C over the same range.

In (a2), the M2 steel panel, the filled-square retained-austenite values are lower than in (a1), lying near 0.25-0.28 below ~650 °C and decaying to about 0.05 at 900 °C, with the Ms curve again reaching ~300 °C.

Both (a1) and (a2) contain a shaded band labelled "Complete Retention of Predicted Equilibrium Austenite fraction" terminated by a vertical dashed line at approximately 650 °C, plus a horizontal dashed line just above 0.0 on the left axis.
Panel (b) legend identifies M1 bars as black and M2 bars as red, with axes Frequency (%) 0-100 and Grain Size (μm) 0.0-3.0.
In (b) roughly 95% of M1 grains and about 92% of M2 grains fall in the bin between ~0.25 and 0.5 μm, so both steels are dominated by very fine grains.
In (b) M2 has a small bar near 1.5 μm (a few percent) that is essentially absent for M1, indicating M2 contains a coarser-grain population.
Panel (c) legend defines the red arrow as Mn, C and the black arrow as Si partitioning direction.
Panel (c) shows for M1 only red Mn/C arrows from α into γ, whereas for M2 additional black Si arrows leave γ into both α and δ-ferrite.

The caption states the retained austenite fractions were calculated with the Koistinen-Marburger model together with calculated Ms temperatures corresponding to the austenite compositions, and that panel (b) gives grain size distributions of M1 and M2 and panel (c) a schematic of elemental partitioning.
The caption labels both (a) sub-panels as "(a) M1 and (a) M2", an evident typographical duplication; the images themselves are labelled a1) and a2).

For the M1-IA sample, the citing text reports an observed retained austenite fraction of ~45% versus a calculated ~16%, attributed to local Mn segregation and a high fraction of grains finer than the 0.5 μm critical size.
For the M2-IA sample, the citing text reports an observed austenite fraction of ~19% against a calculated ~11%, a smaller discrepancy than for M1-IA because the fraction of finer grains is lower.

The citing text explains that below a critical intercritical annealing temperature (where calculated Ms is below RT, the shaded region) the full predicted equilibrium austenite fraction is expected to be retained, while above it retention at RT is always lower than the equilibrium prediction; the IAT of 700 °C used for M1 lies above that critical value.

measured_quantities: calculated retained austenite fraction at RT (%)
unreadable_items: Panels (a1)/(a2): individual marker values are not printed, so retained-austenite fractions and Ms temperatures can only be read to approximately gridline resolution
Panel (a1): left-axis unit is printed as (%) although the tick scale runs 0.0-1.0 (fraction rather than percent)
